Q: problem regarding recursion and backtracking A:

If the constraints allow for a function to be passed as argument, then you could pass a function that prints the partition members that were already selected. For instance, in Python:

# helper function that prints one number and then executes a given function
def print_and_exec(n, func):
    print(n, end=" ")
    func()

def partitions(n, print_rest=print, lo=1):
    for take in range(lo, n // 2 + 1):
        partitions(n - take, lambda: print_and_exec(take, print_rest), take)
    if n >= lo:
        print_and_exec(n, print_rest)

If for instance you call it like this:

partitions(7)

The output will be:

1 1 1 1 1 1 1 
2 1 1 1 1 1 
3 1 1 1 1 
2 2 1 1 1 
4 1 1 1 
3 2 1 1 
5 1 1 
2 2 2 1 
4 2 1 
3 3 1 
6 1 
3 2 2 
5 2 
4 3 
7

But it should be noted that implicitly the functions that are passed as argument really implement a kind of linked list, since they have the recursive print calls embedded within them. On the other hand, recursion itself implies an array, as the arguments and return address of the recursive calls are implicitly put on a stack.

Q: Android Capture Wi-Fi Channel utilization but always return stale/cache value A:

The value you are logging is almost certainly not Channel Utilization, it is the low byte of Station Count. Actually I am not sure why you edited your question deleting relevant part of your code. In the code you had in initial text was:

ByteBuffer data = bytes.order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
// Extract Utilization (3rd byte)
int utilizationRaw = data.get() & 0xFF;

it even indicates to read 3rd byte, but you read the first byte. So to only correct this line you should use this code:

int utilizationRaw = data.get(2) & 0xFF;

The code in:

https://cs.android.com/android/platform/superproject/+/android-latest-release:packages/modules/Wifi/service/java/com/android/server/wifi/util/InformationElementUtil.java;l=332

shows how to properly parse ByteBuffer. Equivalent to what AOSP does there, using the public API:

ByteBuffer data = ie.getBytes().order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
int stationCount       = data.getShort() & 0xFFFF; // bytes 0-1  <- your "9" came from here
int channelUtilization = data.get() & 0xFF;        // byte 2     <- the real value
int capacity  = data.getShort() & 0xFFFF; // bytes 3-4
float busyPercent      = channelUtilization * 100f / 255f;

You may also want to look at how AOSP itself measures utilization, from link-layer stats instead of beacons:

https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/Wifi/+/refs/heads/android16-release/service/java/com/android/server/wifi/WifiChannelUtilization.java

That class is internal to the wifi service, but a privileged system app can get the same counters via the

@SystemApi WifiManager.addOnWifiUsabilityStatsListener(). Use: WifiUsabilityStatsEntry.getTotalCcaBusyFreqTimeMillis() / getTotalRadioOnFreqTimeMillis(), requires the privileged permission WIFI_UPDATE_USABILITY_STATS_SCORE.

See here:

https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/Wifi/+/refs/heads/android16-qpr2-release/framework/java/android/net/wifi/WifiManager.java https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/Wifi/+/refs/heads/main/framework/java/android/net/wifi/WifiUsabilityStatsEntry.java
